text:
maya: Hey team — escalation from ticket #7890 (ACME). Customer reports sudden billing spike and intermittent 403s right after we promoted the canary model gptx-2q around 10:30 UTC. They can reproduce a 403 and tokens charged look ~3x expected. Need repro steps, request IDs, and a debug bundle.

alex: Who's on the account? any request IDs we can trace?

maya: Account is ACME corp (internal ref ticket 7890). First failing req id I have: req_20260315_4572 (~10:32 UTC). I can reproduce locally — posting minimal curl below.

maya: ```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "x-request-id: req_20260315_4572" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-2q","input":"hello
"}'
```

maya: Response body: `{"error":"forbidden","code":403,"detail":"customer limit exceeded"}` — weird because billing UI shows no spike for them at the same time. Also token_counter shows ~450 tokens for that tiny input.

alex: That error text coming from billing-service. Could be an overcounting bug. @sam any ideas?

sam: @alex maybe tokenization change in gptx-2q canary? We've seen tokenizer v3 double-count on trailing-newline edgecases. Also check if request was routed to a quantized path that does a separate token accounting pass.

alex: I'm pulling routing + billing logs for req_20260315_4572. maya, please create a debug bundle so we have traces & logs attached.

maya: debugbot: create_debugbundle ticket=7890 req=req_20260315_4572 include=logs,trace,token_dump

debugbot: created bundle dbg-20260315-88 link: https://internal.redwood/debug/dbg-20260315-88

alex: Quick glance: canary instances are using tokenizer v3, stable uses v2. Token dump shows token_count=452 on canary for that payload vs token_count=15 on stable. That explains billing spike. Also billing-service treats token_count from caller and applies limits — so inflated token_count caused 403.

julie: That's a bad rollout regression. Suggest we immediately pin routes back to stable (gptx-1q or gptx-1q-v2 depending on naming). Customer wants canary disabled.

alex: Two options: rollback canary OR pin route to stable. To pin via API: 
PATCH /v1/routes/route-prod 
Body: {"model":"gptx-1q","pin":"stable","rollout":0}
Or via CLI: `redwood routes update --route route-prod --model gptx-1q --pin stable --rollout 0`

maya: I'm going to pin now and inform customer.

maya: pinned route-prod to gptx-1q (rollout=0) @1933334500 :white_check_mark:

sam: After pinning, monitor for 403s and token counts. Also check regional propagation — some replicas lag.

maya: Customer reports fewer 403s immediately but they still saw one at 10:45. Sending that req id: req_20260315_4710.

alex: That one hit a regional replica that didn't get the pin before the 5-min propagation window expired. Looks like the replica was still serving the canary bundle. We'll accelerate propagation and add a temporary sync flag.

alex: PATCH /v1/configs/routing 
Body: {"sync_across_regions":true,"propagation_timeout":60}

maya: Applied routing sync change. Also added a short-term fallback rule: if any model variant returns 403 or 5xx, route to stable gptx-1q.

maya: Fallback config: `{"fallback":{"on_status":[403,500,502,503],"target":"gptx-1q"}}` — enabled.

sam: That should stop customer-facing 403s while we investigate thorough root cause. For the postmortem, we need a repro kit: tokenization diffs, sample inputs that trigger doubling, kernel/quantization path, and metrics showing token_count delta.

alex: I'll attach tokenized inputs + token counts to dbg-20260315-88 and add links to routing logs and billing audit.

debugbot: updated bundle dbg-20260315-88 with attachments (token_dump.log, routing_trace.json, billing_audit.csv)

maya: Customer updated: we've pinned to stable and enabled fallback; we've collected a debug bundle and will follow up with timeline + next steps. They asked for ETA for permanent fix.

julie: Product asks ML infra to prioritize a patch: revert tokenizer v3 behavior that changes tokenization semantics or coordinate model config to use v2 tokenizer until v3 is validated.

sam: Agreed. We'll schedule a hotfix for canary quantization/tokenization path tomorrow morning. Also adding an automatic check in rollout tests: token_count sanity check (diff vs stable < 20%).

alex: For internal handoff to model onboarding: sample inputs that reproduce (attached) + tokenization diffs + debug bundle link.

maya: Closing the immediate customer loop. Moving a summary to #postmortems with the debug bundle link and roll-back notes.

maya: Summary (for the thread): cause = tokenizer change in canary -> inflated token counts -> billing-service triggered 403. Mitigation = pinned to stable, enabled fallback + routing sync. Follow-ups = patch tokenizer or pin model until validated, add token_count rollout check.

maya: closing thread, will open postmortem doc in #postmortems. :pray:
